CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding - low hemoglobin.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Stephanie is a 49-year-old female presenting for evaluation of low hemoglobin. Over the past couple of months, she has experienced significant fatigue and dizziness. She reports that activities she previously performed daily, such as walking a mile or going to work, now leave her worn out and tired. She denies blood in stools, dark or tarry stools, heavy menstrual bleeding, weight loss, loss of appetite, or syncope. She did have blood in stools approximately three years ago, which prompted a colonoscopy at that time, but has had no similar episodes since. She notes some leg swelling recently, which she attributes to increased salt intake while traveling. She denies shortness of breath or problems lying flat at night. Regarding her kidney stones from a couple of years ago, she denies recent flare-ups, back pain, flank pain, or hematuria.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports mild nasal congestion attributed to seasonal allergies with changing seasons. Denies fever, chills, sore throat, or cough.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, kidney stones, diverticulosis (found on colonoscopy three years ago), prior colonoscopy.

MEDICATIONS
Toprol 50 milligrams daily, Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports recent travel to Vermont. Acknowledges dietary indiscretion with increased fast food consumption and difficulty maintaining salt restriction due to travel.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure and heart rate normal. Cardiac exam: 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, consistent with prior findings. Lower extremities: Trace to 1+ pitting edema in ankles.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from six months ago shows ejection fraction of 45% and moderate mitral regurgitation. Hemoglobin: 8.2 (low).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. New anemia: Send anemia profile to determine type of anemia. Refer to gastroenterology for evaluation, likely to include endoscopy and colonoscopy.
2. Congestive heart failure: Start Lasix 40 milligrams once daily for fluid retention. Continue Toprol 50 milligrams daily and Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Counsel on strict salt restriction. Obtain scale and weigh daily. Instruct to call if weight increases, as may require adjustment of diuretic dose.
3. Kidney stones: Continue current management. Maintain hydration and watchful diet despite diuretic use. Call with any questions.
